summary: Dietary fiber is carbohydrate that is not readily digested in the small intestine; soluble and insoluble forms have different properties.

foodSourceRules.notes: Exact published Phase 07 source profiles only; missing measurements are not zero. State, units and serving mass remain explicit.

absorptionFactors.description: FDA describes soluble fiber forming a gel and being broken down by intestinal bacteria, while insoluble fiber passes relatively intact. These are broad distinctions, not a guaranteed response to every fiber ingredient.

deficiency.overview: FDA describes fiber in relation to bowel function and diet quality; this does not diagnose a deficiency or the cause of bowel symptoms.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: This source is not an individual digestive-tolerance assessment and supplies no universal fiber toxicity threshold.
excess.medicalBoundary: No upper limit is an intake goal. Individual clinical or medical assessment requires a qualified professional.
